mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel engine replacement typically costs £4,000-£6,500 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, or £2,800-£5,000 for a reconditioned engine, depending on the specific engine code (D5244T family or B4204T Drive-E). Used engine options start from around £1,800. Supply and fit adds approximately 10-14 hours of labour at specialist rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of D5 injector failure in a Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include rough idling, poor acceleration, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, increased fuel consumption, and engine management warning lights. Cold-start issues and a strong diesel smell from the engine bay are also typical indicators of injector seal failure (the 'black death' carbon buildup).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends entirely on the vehicle's condition and value. For a first-generation XC90 D5 worth £3,000-£6,000, a used engine or targeted repair (injectors, EGR) typically makes better financial sense. For second-generation XC90 D4 models worth £12,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment if the car is otherwise in good condition.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel engine replacement takes 2-3 days for the engine swap itself, depending on the workshop's workload. For D5 five-cylinder units, access is relatively straightforward; B4204T Drive-E units in the SPA chassis are also well-supported. Allow additional time for diagnostics and final checks.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the D4 and D5 diesel engines in the Volvo XC90?

acceptedAnswer.text: The D5 badge traditionally denotes Volvo's 2.4-litre five-cylinder turbo diesel (D5244T family), producing 163-200hp depending on variant, fitted to first-generation XC90s (2002-2014). The D4 badge on second-generation XC90s (2015-present) covers the 2.0-litre four-cylinder Drive-E diesel (B4204T family), producing 190hp with improved emissions and fuel economy.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine unit against manufacturing defects and failure, providing peace of mind for one of the most significant repairs an XC90 owner can undertake. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel covers two distinct engine generations across the first-generation P2 chassis (2002-2014) and second-generation SPA chassis (2015-present). The D5 badge originally denoted Volvo's 2.4-litre five-cylinder diesel, while the D4 badge arrived with the second-generation's Drive-E four-cylinder family - both sharing the same "D4-D5 Diesel" page due to body-style scope.

milestones.description: D5244T (2.4-litre five-cylinder turbo diesel, 163hp) launched with the original XC90
D5244T4 introduced (185hp) with improved common-rail injection
D5244T5 added (200hp, twin-turbo) for higher-output D5 variants
D5244T18 introduced (200hp) with stop-start and improved emissions
Second-generation XC90 launches; B4204T11 (2.0-litre four-cylinder twin-turbo diesel, 190hp) replaces the five-cylinder D5
B4204T23 (190hp, updated emissions hardware) introduced alongside mild-hybrid preparation

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volvo XC90 D4-D5 Diesel - particularly the five-cylinder D5244T family and the later Drive-E B4204T units - has known failure patterns that owners should understand. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: D5 Injector & EGR System Failures - Why the Volvo XC90 D5 Diesel Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The common-rail injection system on five-cylinder D5 units suffers from injector seal failure (carbon blow-by) and EGR cooler blockages, leading to performance loss and increased emissions. Swirl flap failure in the inlet manifold is also common on higher-mileage examples.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of injectors and seals; EGR cleaning
repairOptions.longevity: Prevents further damage; suitable for 80,000+ mile cars

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When multiple failures coincide or engine is high-mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: First-generation XC90 D5 values typically sit between £3,000-£10,000 depending on age and mileage. If your XC90 D5 is worth under £5,000, injector replacement or a used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. For vehicles worth £5,000-£8,000, evaluate both options; a reconditioned unit is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. For £8,000+ examples, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: If your D5 is exhibiting injector or EGR problems and the vehicle is otherwise sound, injector replacement is often the more cost-effective route. However, if swirl flaps have failed or the engine is beyond 150,000 miles with multiple concurrent issues, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components is the more sensible long-term investment.

problems.h4: Drive-E Turbo & AdBlue System Failures - Why the Volvo XC90 D4 Diesel Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The B4204T family's turbocharger wastegate actuators can fail (causing power loss and engine management lights), while AdBlue system components (NOx sensors, heaters) and EGR coolers are known weak points on higher-mileage examples.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early; prevents turbo damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When turbo damage has occurred or engine high-mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Second-generation XC90 D4 values typically sit between £12,000-£40,000 depending on age and mileage. Replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value for most examples, making a reconditioned or rebuilt unit a financially sensible option for owners planning to keep the car.
problems.recommendation: For the B4204T family, early intervention on turbo actuator issues is critical - catching the problem before turbo damage occurs saves significant cost. If the turbo has already failed or the engine is high-mileage with multiple issues, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components is the recommended route.
